mcp.name: biomate_session
mcp.title: Run BioMate Session
mcp.description:
**Primary entry point — use this for 90% of requests.** Run a complete BioMate scientific session from a natural-language goal. BioMate selects the right workflow from 2,455 indexed pipelines, pre-fills parameters from your goal text, executes on BioMate cloud, handles QC gates with auto-loop remediation, and produces structured findings. While running, the tool streams real-time progress (phase started, step completed, QC gate, auto-loop remediation, finding) back to the host. Returns a final run summary, a deep link to the live results panel, and the report URL. 

**How to write the `goal` parameter** — plain English, one to three sentences:
• Include the *what*: analysis type + subject (e.g. 'ADMET screening', 'RNA-seq DE', 'variant calling')
• Include *data location*: inline SMILES/sequences, S3 paths, accession numbers, or upload first with upload_file
• Include key *parameters* that matter: organism, library type, comparisons, thresholds
• You can omit anything BioMate can infer (it will ask if genuinely ambiguous)

**Good examples:**
  'Screen aspirin (CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O) and caffeine (Cn1cnc2c1c(=O)n(c(=O)n2C)C) for hERG inhibition, CYP3A4, and oral bioavailability'
  'RNA-seq differential expression on s3://lab-bucket/exp42/fastqs/ — human GRCh38, dUTP strand-specific, treated (n=3) vs control (n=3), FDR 0.05'
  'Whole-genome variant calling on the uploaded FASTQ pair, GRCh38, GATK HaplotypeCaller, germline mode'
  'Run homogeneous 3D refinement in CryoSPARC on s3://cryo/job042/, C2 symmetry, box size 256'
  'Fetch GSE183947 from GEO and run the same RNA-seq pipeline'

Use run_workflow instead when the user wants to call a specific workflow by ID with explicit parameter control.

goal.description: Natural-language scientific goal. Include: analysis type, data location (inline SMILES/sequences, s3:// paths, or GEO/SRA accession numbers), and key parameters (organism, comparisons, thresholds). BioMate infers the rest. Examples: 'Screen these 5 SMILES for hERG IC50 and CYP3A4 inhibition', 'RNA-seq DE on s3://bucket/exp1/ human GRCh38 paired-end treated vs control', 'Fetch GSE183947 and run differential expression'.

experiment_id.description: Optional experiment to attach this run to (from recall_memory).

stream.description: Emit progress notifications during execution. Default true. Set false for hosts without MCP notification support — then poll with get_run.

mcp.name: search_workflow
mcp.title: Search Workflows
mcp.description: Search the BioMate workflow catalog (2,455 indexed workflows across 34 domains) by natural language. Returns ranked workflow cards with id, name, domain, one-line description, and estimated BioMate cloud cost. Use this when the user wants to pick a workflow explicitly; otherwise prefer biomate_session.

query.description: Natural language description of the analysis.

domain.description: Optional domain filter: transcriptomics, genomics, proteomics, drug_discovery, cryo_em, etc.

mcp.name: get_workflow_spec
mcp.title: Get Workflow Spec
mcp.description: Return the full specification for a workflow: required + optional parameters (with types and allowed values), default QC profile and thresholds, expected input files, estimated cost and runtime, and any license requirements. Call this before run_workflow when the user wants explicit parameter control.

mcp.name: run_workflow
mcp.title: Run Workflow
mcp.description: Execute a specific BioMate workflow on BioMate cloud with explicit parameters. Returns a run_id immediately. If stream=true, also emits progress notifications until the run terminates (same events as biomate_session). Use biomate_session instead when the user gave you a natural-language goal.

params.description: Parameter dict. Required params come from get_workflow_spec.

stream.description: Emit progress notifications while running. Default false.

mcp.name: watch_run
mcp.description: Stream real-time progress for a running BioMate workflow and return full results when done. Emits MCP notifications/progress for every phase start/complete, step update, and QC gate. When the run finishes, automatically fetches output files (with download URLs) and AI findings. Use after run_workflow (non-streaming) to watch a submitted run. Does not require re-submitting — takes an existing run_id.

mcp.name: get_run
mcp.title: Get Run Details
mcp.description: Return everything about a run in one call: status (pending|running|completed|failed), per-phase and per-step progress with timestamps, output files with download URLs, structured findings, QC gate results, and any auto-loop remediations applied. Replaces get_run_status + get_run_results + step-level findings polling.

mcp.name: cancel_run
mcp.title: Cancel Run
mcp.description: Cancel a running or queued BioMate workflow on BioMate cloud.

mcp.name: list_runs
mcp.title: List Runs
mcp.description: List the user's recent runs with status and timestamps. Filter by status or experiment.

mcp.name: preview_file
mcp.title: Preview Output File
mcp.description: Render a server-side preview of an output file (FASTA, VCF, CSV/TSV, image, PDF). Returns markdown + optional thumbnail PNG. Use this to show the user what an output looks like without downloading multi-GB files. For input QC of files the user is about to upload, prefer biomate_session (it runs a real QC workflow).

s3_key.description: The full s3_uri value (must start with 's3://') copied verbatim from a get_run output_files entry — e.g. 's3://bucket/path/file.json'. NOT a bare key; the s3:// prefix is required.

mcp.name: export_report
mcp.title: Export Report
mcp.description: Render a publication-ready report for a completed run as PDF or markdown. Includes the methods section, QC audit trail, structured findings, and figures. This is what users need for IND submissions, CRO compliance packages, and publication supplementary materials.

mcp.name: analyze_results
mcp.title: Analyze Results
mcp.description: Ask BioMate's AI to interpret a completed run. Returns natural-language analysis: key findings, quality assessment, scientific interpretation, recommended next steps. Use after get_run when the user asks 'what does this mean?'.

mcp.name: explain_error
mcp.title: Explain Run Error
mcp.description: Diagnose a failed run. Returns the likely root cause (genome mismatch, missing input, OOM, container pull failure, etc.) and the specific fix. Often the next step is run_workflow with corrected params.

mcp.name: query_database
mcp.title: Query Biological Database
mcp.description: Query a biological/chemical database by accession or name. Use database='federated' to fan out across all sources simultaneously and merge results. Single-source options: uniprot, pdb, pdbe, alphafold, ncbi_gene, dbsnp, clinvar, gnomad, kegg, reactome, chebi, chembl, pubchem, bindingdb, pharos, hpo, string, pubmed.

database.description: Database to query. Use 'federated' to query all sources in parallel.

query.description: Accession, gene symbol, compound name, or free text.

operation.description: Search mode chosen from user intent: 'lookup' (by ID/name, default), 'similarity' (chembl/pubchem=chemical similarity over SMILES; pdb=sequence homologs over the whole PDB), or 'text' (keyword search).

entity_type.description: Hint for federated routing: gene, protein, variant, compound, pathway, disease, or omit to auto-detect.

mcp.name: resolve_accession
mcp.title: Resolve Accession
mcp.description: Identify a public archive accession (GEO, SRA, ENA, DDBJ) and return the best BioMate workflow to fetch it plus pre-filled params ready for run_workflow. Examples: GSE183947 → Geo Data Connector; SRR12345 → nf-core/fetchngs. Call this before run_workflow whenever the user provides an accession instead of a file.

accession.description: Public archive accession: GSE*, GSM*, GDS*, SRR*, SRX*, SRP*, ERR*, ERX*, ERP*, DRR*, PRJNA*, PRJEB*, E-MTAB-*, E-GEOD-*

mcp.name: browse_data
mcp.title: Browse Data Repository
mcp.description: Browse a biological data repository or S3 workspace by listing files and directories at a given path. Public sources (EBI, NCBI, Ensembl, UCSC) require a path. S3 sources (biomate_workspace, user_s3) accept an optional prefix. Use before fetch_public_data to navigate to the exact file you need.

source_id.description: Data source to browse. biomate_workspace = BioMate's S3 work bucket; user_s3 = user's own S3 bucket (if configured).

path.description: Directory path or S3 prefix to list (e.g. '/pub/databases/uniprot/' or 'results/run-xyz/').

mcp.name: fetch_public_data
mcp.title: Fetch Public Data
mcp.description: Download a file from a public biological repository (EBI, NCBI, Ensembl, UCSC) into BioMate's S3 workspace and return a presigned URL and S3 URI. Use the S3 URI as a workflow input parameter. Call browse_data first to find the exact path.

source_id.description: Data source the file comes from.

url.description: For http_public source: full HTTPS URL of the file to download.

mcp.name: recall_memory
mcp.title: Recall Memory
mcp.description: Retrieve relevant prior context for the current goal: past runs on similar inputs, validated procedures, findings tagged by the user, learned parameter preferences. Call before biomate_session for repeat users — it dramatically improves param auto-fill and avoids re-running work.

query.description: What to recall — usually the user's goal.

mcp.name: search_literature
mcp.title: Search Literature
mcp.description: Search published scientific literature across PubMed, EuropePMC, Semantic Scholar, and OpenAlex. Uses an iterative depth-loop: starts broad, then drills into related topics until min_results are found or max_depth is reached. Returns ranked papers with title, authors, year, DOI, abstract snippet, and citation count. Best for: finding prior art, understanding a disease mechanism, locating validation datasets, or reviewing methods before running a workflow.

query.description: Natural-language search query. Be specific: include organism, assay type, or drug name. E.g. 'DESeq2 bulk RNA-seq breast cancer ER+ 2020-2024'.

max_depth.description: How many iterative refinement rounds to run (1–4). Higher = more thorough, slower.

min_results.description: Stop when at least this many papers are found.

mcp.name: upload_file
mcp.title: Upload File
mcp.description:
Get a one-shot signed S3 PUT URL so the host can upload a local file directly to BioMate's data plane without proxying bytes through the chat transport. For files >5MB this is mandatory; for small text payloads, inline strings are fine.

**Returns** `{upload_url, s3_key}` — two fields:
- `upload_url`: a presigned HTTPS URL. You MUST upload the file bytes to it with an HTTP PUT before calling any other tool: `curl -X PUT -T <local_path> "<upload_url>"`
- `s3_key`: a bare S3 object key (e.g. `users/42/uploads/uuid-sample.fastq.gz`). Pass this value directly into the `inputs` dict of `biomate_session` or as a `params` value in `run_workflow` — BioMate resolves the bucket internally. Example: `inputs={"fastq_file": s3_key}` or `params={"input": s3_key}`.

**Full upload workflow:**
1. `upload_file(filename='sample.fastq.gz', size_bytes=52000000)` → get `upload_url` + `s3_key`
2. `curl -X PUT -T sample.fastq.gz "<upload_url>"` (or equivalent HTTP PUT — no auth header needed)
3. `biomate_session(goal='Run RNA-seq DE on the uploaded FASTQs, human GRCh38', inputs={"fastq_file": s3_key})`

content_type.description: MIME type (auto-detected from filename if omitted).

mcp.name: list_instruments
mcp.title: List Lab Instruments
mcp.description: Discover lab instruments reachable on the local network (currently OpenTrons OT-2/Flex liquid-handling robots). Returns each robot's IP, name, model, and health. Runs locally — only works when the MCP server is on the same network as the instruments. Set the OPENTRONS_ROBOT_IPS env var or pass `ips` to skip network scanning.

ips.description: Explicit robot IPs to probe (e.g. ['192.168.1.42']). Omit to use OPENTRONS_ROBOT_IPS.

mcp.name: get_instrument_status
mcp.title: Get Instrument Status
mcp.description: Get the status of a run on a lab instrument (OpenTrons). Returns status ('idle'|'running'|'paused'|'succeeded'|'failed'|'stopped'), timestamps, and any errors. Poll this after run_instrument_protocol.

robot_ip.description: IP of the robot running the protocol.

mcp.name: run_instrument_protocol
mcp.title: Run Instrument Protocol
mcp.description: Execute a liquid-handling protocol on an OpenTrons robot. **Physical action — actuates real hardware.** Two-step guardrail: called with `confirm=false` (the DEFAULT) it performs a DRY RUN — compiles and returns the exact protocol that WOULD run, WITHOUT contacting or actuating the robot. Review it, then call again with `confirm=true` to verify reachability, upload, and physically start the run. Provide either raw `protocol_code` (a valid OT-2/Flex Python protocol) or a structured `transfers` spec (source/dest labware + pipette + well transfers), which is compiled into a protocol for you. Returns {protocol_id, run_id, status}; poll get_instrument_status to follow the run.

confirm.description: MUST be true to physically run. false (default) = dry-run preview only, no actuation.

protocol_code.description: Full OT-2/Flex Python protocol source. Omit if using `transfers`.

protocol_name.description: Filename on the robot (must end in .py).

transfers.description: Structured well-to-well transfers; compiled to a protocol when protocol_code is omitted.

source_labware.description: OT-2 labware for the source plate (required with `transfers`).

dest_labware.description: OT-2 labware for the destination plate (required with `transfers`).

mcp.name: design_candidates
mcp.title: Design Cyclic-Peptide Candidates
mcp.description: Design (in-silico) — generate a library of candidate cyclic (macrocyclic) peptides for a design goal. Enumerates head-to-tail cyclic peptides over an amino-acid alphabet with controllable N-methylation, returning each candidate's sequence, residues, N-methylation count/positions, and a ready-to-use cyclic SMILES. This is the Design step of the DBTL loop — feed its output straight into score_candidates to prioritize what to synthesize. Runs locally; requires RDKit in the connector runtime.

length.description: Residues per macrocycle: a fixed int, or a [min,max] range to sample.

max_nmethyl.description: Cap on N-methylations per peptide (N-Me is expensive to synthesize).

alphabet.description: Residue names to sample (e.g. ['Ala','Leu','Phe']). Omit for the lipophilic-leaning default alphabet.

seed.description: RNG seed — vary between rounds to draw a fresh batch.

mcp.name: score_candidates
mcp.title: Score Cyclic-Peptide Permeability
mcp.description: Test (in-silico property prediction) — predict membrane permeability (log Papp) for candidate cyclic peptides using the production HistGBM scorer over RDKit descriptors (the model that won the scaffold-split head-to-heads). Accepts the output of design_candidates (or raw SMILES) and returns candidates ranked by predicted permeability, descending, so the host can prioritize what to synthesize. Runs locally; requires RDKit and the pickled model at BIOMATE_PERM_SCORER_PKL (sync from s3://knowledge-datasets-1759951976/cyclic_peptide/scorer/).

mcp.name: propose_next_round
mcp.title: Propose Next DBTL Round
mcp.description: Learn + Decide — given measured assay results from the last synthesized batch, decide whether to PROCEED (target met), REFINE (adjust design params and keep going), or PIVOT (flat rounds → change strategy), and return the next design parameters to synthesize. This is the Learn step that closes the DBTL loop between wet-lab results and the next design round. One-shot: it decides from the aggregate metric of the batch you pass; multi-round PIVOT detection (needs iteration history) requires the orchestrated run_dbtl_loop tool. Runs locally, no compute job.

results.description: Prior batch: each candidate and its measured value.

measured_metric.description: Its measured value (e.g. logPapp, KD, or hit indicator).

objective.description: How to aggregate results into the decision metric.

target.description: Target metric (e.g. hit-fraction 0.3, or a logPapp cutoff).

max_no_improve.description: Flat rounds before PIVOT (only fires with iteration history — see run_dbtl_loop).

params.description: Current design params to advance (round, perm_threshold, explore, …). Optional.

function.name: search_workflow
function.description: Search the BioMate workflow catalog (2,455 indexed workflows across 34 domains) by natural language. Returns ranked workflow cards with id, name, domain, one-line description, and estimated BioMate cloud cost. Use this when the user wants to pick a workflow explicitly; otherwise prefer biomate_session.

query.description: Natural language description of the analysis.

domain.description: Optional domain filter: transcriptomics, genomics, proteomics, drug_discovery, cryo_em, etc.

function.name: get_workflow_spec
function.description: Return the full specification for a workflow: required + optional parameters (with types and allowed values), default QC profile and thresholds, expected input files, estimated cost and runtime, and any license requirements. Call this before run_workflow when the user wants explicit parameter control.

function.name: run_workflow
function.description: Execute a specific BioMate workflow on BioMate cloud with explicit parameters. Returns a run_id immediately. If stream=true, also emits progress notifications until the run terminates (same events as biomate_session). Use biomate_session instead when the user gave you a natural-language goal.

params.description: Parameter dict. Required params come from get_workflow_spec.

stream.description: Emit progress notifications while running. Default false.

function.name: watch_run
function.description: Stream real-time progress for a running BioMate workflow and return full results when done. Emits MCP notifications/progress for every phase start/complete, step update, and QC gate. When the run finishes, automatically fetches output files (with download URLs) and AI findings. Use after run_workflow (non-streaming) to watch a submitted run. Does not require re-submitting — takes an existing run_id.

function.name: get_run
function.description: Return everything about a run in one call: status (pending|running|completed|failed), per-phase and per-step progress with timestamps, output files with download URLs, structured findings, QC gate results, and any auto-loop remediations applied. Replaces get_run_status + get_run_results + step-level findings polling.

function.name: cancel_run
function.description: Cancel a running or queued BioMate workflow on BioMate cloud.

function.name: list_runs
function.description: List the user's recent runs with status and timestamps. Filter by status or experiment.

function.name: preview_file
function.description: Render a server-side preview of an output file (FASTA, VCF, CSV/TSV, image, PDF). Returns markdown + optional thumbnail PNG. Use this to show the user what an output looks like without downloading multi-GB files. For input QC of files the user is about to upload, prefer biomate_session (it runs a real QC workflow).

s3_key.description: The full s3_uri value (must start with 's3://') copied verbatim from a get_run output_files entry — e.g. 's3://bucket/path/file.json'. NOT a bare key; the s3:// prefix is required.

function.name: export_report
function.description: Render a publication-ready report for a completed run as PDF or markdown. Includes the methods section, QC audit trail, structured findings, and figures. This is what users need for IND submissions, CRO compliance packages, and publication supplementary materials.

function.name: analyze_results
function.description: Ask BioMate's AI to interpret a completed run. Returns natural-language analysis: key findings, quality assessment, scientific interpretation, recommended next steps. Use after get_run when the user asks 'what does this mean?'.

function.name: explain_error
function.description: Diagnose a failed run. Returns the likely root cause (genome mismatch, missing input, OOM, container pull failure, etc.) and the specific fix. Often the next step is run_workflow with corrected params.

function.name: query_database
function.description: Query a biological/chemical database by accession or name. Use database='federated' to fan out across all sources simultaneously and merge results. Single-source options: uniprot, pdb, pdbe, alphafold, ncbi_gene, dbsnp, clinvar, gnomad, kegg, reactome, chebi, chembl, pubchem, bindingdb, pharos, hpo, string, pubmed.

database.description: Database to query. Use 'federated' to query all sources in parallel.

query.description: Accession, gene symbol, compound name, or free text.

operation.description: Search mode chosen from user intent: 'lookup' (by ID/name, default), 'similarity' (chembl/pubchem=chemical similarity over SMILES; pdb=sequence homologs over the whole PDB), or 'text' (keyword search).

entity_type.description: Hint for federated routing: gene, protein, variant, compound, pathway, disease, or omit to auto-detect.

function.name: resolve_accession
function.description: Identify a public archive accession (GEO, SRA, ENA, DDBJ) and return the best BioMate workflow to fetch it plus pre-filled params ready for run_workflow. Examples: GSE183947 → Geo Data Connector; SRR12345 → nf-core/fetchngs. Call this before run_workflow whenever the user provides an accession instead of a file.

accession.description: Public archive accession: GSE*, GSM*, GDS*, SRR*, SRX*, SRP*, ERR*, ERX*, ERP*, DRR*, PRJNA*, PRJEB*, E-MTAB-*, E-GEOD-*

function.name: browse_data
function.description: Browse a biological data repository or S3 workspace by listing files and directories at a given path. Public sources (EBI, NCBI, Ensembl, UCSC) require a path. S3 sources (biomate_workspace, user_s3) accept an optional prefix. Use before fetch_public_data to navigate to the exact file you need.

source_id.description: Data source to browse. biomate_workspace = BioMate's S3 work bucket; user_s3 = user's own S3 bucket (if configured).

path.description: Directory path or S3 prefix to list (e.g. '/pub/databases/uniprot/' or 'results/run-xyz/').

function.name: fetch_public_data
function.description: Download a file from a public biological repository (EBI, NCBI, Ensembl, UCSC) into BioMate's S3 workspace and return a presigned URL and S3 URI. Use the S3 URI as a workflow input parameter. Call browse_data first to find the exact path.

source_id.description: Data source the file comes from.

url.description: For http_public source: full HTTPS URL of the file to download.

function.name: recall_memory
function.description: Retrieve relevant prior context for the current goal: past runs on similar inputs, validated procedures, findings tagged by the user, learned parameter preferences. Call before biomate_session for repeat users — it dramatically improves param auto-fill and avoids re-running work.

query.description: What to recall — usually the user's goal.

function.name: search_literature
function.description: Search published scientific literature across PubMed, EuropePMC, Semantic Scholar, and OpenAlex. Uses an iterative depth-loop: starts broad, then drills into related topics until min_results are found or max_depth is reached. Returns ranked papers with title, authors, year, DOI, abstract snippet, and citation count. Best for: finding prior art, understanding a disease mechanism, locating validation datasets, or reviewing methods before running a workflow.

query.description: Natural-language search query. Be specific: include organism, assay type, or drug name. E.g. 'DESeq2 bulk RNA-seq breast cancer ER+ 2020-2024'.

max_depth.description: How many iterative refinement rounds to run (1–4). Higher = more thorough, slower.

min_results.description: Stop when at least this many papers are found.

function.name: upload_file
function.description:
Get a one-shot signed S3 PUT URL so the host can upload a local file directly to BioMate's data plane without proxying bytes through the chat transport. For files >5MB this is mandatory; for small text payloads, inline strings are fine.

**Returns** `{upload_url, s3_key}` — two fields:
- `upload_url`: a presigned HTTPS URL. You MUST upload the file bytes to it with an HTTP PUT before calling any other tool: `curl -X PUT -T <local_path> "<upload_url>"`
- `s3_key`: a bare S3 object key (e.g. `users/42/uploads/uuid-sample.fastq.gz`). Pass this value directly into the `inputs` dict of `biomate_session` or as a `params` value in `run_workflow` — BioMate resolves the bucket internally. Example: `inputs={"fastq_file": s3_key}` or `params={"input": s3_key}`.

**Full upload workflow:**
1. `upload_file(filename='sample.fastq.gz', size_bytes=52000000)` → get `upload_url` + `s3_key`
2. `curl -X PUT -T sample.fastq.gz "<upload_url>"` (or equivalent HTTP PUT — no auth header needed)
3. `biomate_session(goal='Run RNA-seq DE on the uploaded FASTQs, human GRCh38', inputs={"fastq_file": s3_key})`

mcp.name: biomate_session
mcp.title: Run BioMate Session
mcp.description:
**Primary entry point — use this for 90% of requests.** Run a complete BioMate scientific session from a natural-language goal. BioMate selects the right workflow from 2,455 indexed pipelines, pre-fills parameters from your goal text, executes on BioMate cloud, handles QC gates with auto-loop remediation, and produces structured findings. While running, the tool streams real-time progress (phase started, step completed, QC gate, auto-loop remediation, finding) back to the host. Returns a final run summary, a deep link to the live results panel, and the report URL. 

**How to write the `goal` parameter** — plain English, one to three sentences:
• Include the *what*: analysis type + subject (e.g. 'ADMET screening', 'RNA-seq DE', 'variant calling')
• Include *data location*: inline SMILES/sequences, S3 paths, accession numbers, or upload first with upload_file
• Include key *parameters* that matter: organism, library type, comparisons, thresholds
• You can omit anything BioMate can infer (it will ask if genuinely ambiguous)

**Good examples:**
  'Screen aspirin (CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O) and caffeine (Cn1cnc2c1c(=O)n(c(=O)n2C)C) for hERG inhibition, CYP3A4, and oral bioavailability'
  'RNA-seq differential expression on s3://lab-bucket/exp42/fastqs/ — human GRCh38, dUTP strand-specific, treated (n=3) vs control (n=3), FDR 0.05'
  'Whole-genome variant calling on the uploaded FASTQ pair, GRCh38, GATK HaplotypeCaller, germline mode'
  'Run homogeneous 3D refinement in CryoSPARC on s3://cryo/job042/, C2 symmetry, box size 256'
  'Fetch GSE183947 from GEO and run the same RNA-seq pipeline'

Use run_workflow instead when the user wants to call a specific workflow by ID with explicit parameter control.
